source_text: Sed luceant, inquit, opera uestra. at nunc lucent tabernae et ianuae nostrae. plures iam inuenias ethnicorum fores sine lucernis et laureis, quam Christianorum. de ista quoque specie quid uidetur ? si idoli honor est, sine dubio idoli honor idololatria est. si hominis causa est, recogitemus omnem idololatrian in hominis causam esse. recogitemus omnem idololatrian in homines esse culturam, cum ipsos deos nationum homines retro fuisse etiam apud suos constet. itaque nihil interest, superioris an huius saeculi uiris superstitio ista praestetur. idololatria non propter personas, quae opponuntur, sed propter officia ista damnata est, quae ad daemonas pertinent. reddenda sunt Caesari quae sunt Caesaris. bene quod apposuit: et quae sunt dei deo. quae ergo sunt Caesaris? scilicet de quibus tunc consultatio mouebatur, praestandusne esset census Caesari an non. ideo et monetam ostendi sibi dominus postulauit et de imagine, cuius esset, requisiuit, et cum audisset Caesaris, reddite, ait, quae sunt Caesaris Caesari, et quae sunt dei deo, id est imaginem Caesaris Caesari, quae in nummo est, et imaginem dei deo, quae in homine est, ut Caesari quidem pecuniam reddas, deo temetipsum. alioquin quid erit dei, si omnia Caesaris? ergo, inquis, honor.. dei est lucernae pro foribus et laurus in postibus ? non utique quod dei honor est, sed quod eius, qui pro deo eiusmodi officiis honoratur, quantum in manifesto est, salua operatione, quae est in occulto, ad daemonia perueniens. certi enim esse debemus, si quos latet per ignorantiam litteraturae saecularis, etiam ostiorum deos apud Romanos, Cardeam a cardinibus appellatam et Forculum a foribus et Limentinum a limine et ipsum Ianum a ianua: et utique scimus, licet nomina inania atque conficta sint, cum tamen in superstitionem deducuntur, rapere ad se daemonia et omnem spiritum inmundum per consecrationis obligamentum. alioquin daemonia nullum habent nomen singillatim, sed ibi nomen inueniunt, ubi et pignus. etiam apud Graecos Apollinem Thyraeum et Antelios daemonas ostiorum praesides legimus. haec igitur ab initio praeuidens spiritus sanctus etiam ostia in superstitionem uentura praececinit per antiquissimum propheten Enoch. nam et alia ostia in balneis adorari uidemus. si autem sunt qui in ostiis adorentur, ad eos et lucernae et laureae pertinebunt. idolo feceris, quicquid ostio feceris. hoc in loco ex auctoritate quoque dei contestor, quia nec tutum est subtrahere, quodcumque uni fuerit ostensum utique omnium causa. scio fratrem per uisionem eadem nocte castigatum grauiter, quod ianuam eius subito adnuntiatis gaudiis publicis serui coronassent. et tamen non ipse coronauerat aut praeceperat; nam ante processerat et regressus reprehenderat factum. adeo apud deum in huiusmodi etiam disciplina familiae nostrae aestimamur. igitur quod attineat ad honores regum uel imperatorum, satis praescriptum habemus, in omni obsequio esse nos oportere secundum apostoli praeceptum subditos magistratibus et principibus et potestatibus, sed intra limites disciplinae, quousque ab idololatria separamur. propterea enim et illud exemplum trium fratrum praecucurrit, qui alias obsequentes erga regem Nabuchodonosor honorem imaginis eius constantissime respuerunt probantes idololatrian esse, quicquid ultra humani honoris modum ad instar diuinae sublimitatis extollitur. sic et Daniel cetera Dario subnixus tamdiu fuit in officio, quamdiu a periculo disciplinae uacaret. nam ne id subiret, non magis leones regios timuit, quam illi regios ignes. accendant igitur quotidie lucernas, quibus lux nulla est, affigant postibus lauros postmodum arsuras, quibus ignes imminent; illis competunt et testimonia tenebrarum et auspicia poenarum. Tu lumen es mundi et arbor uirens semper. si templis renuntiasti, ne feceris templum ianuam tuam. minus dixi: si lupanaribus renuntiasti, ne indueris domui tuae faciem noui lupanaris.
thought_title: Lamps and laurels at the doors
orientation: Tertullian is addressing Christians who decorate their doors with lamps and laurels for public festivals, and he is arguing that even these door-honors belong to idolatry.
pass_a_gloss: But let your works shine, he says. But now our shops and our doors shine. You may already find more doors of pagans without lamps and laurels than of Christians. About this kind also what is seen? If it is an honor of an idol, without doubt an honor of an idol is idolatry. If it is for the sake of a man, let us recall that all idolatry is for the sake of a man. Let us recall that all idolatry is worship toward men, since the very gods of the nations were formerly men, as is established even among their own people. And so it makes no difference whether this superstition is offered to men of an earlier or of this age. Idolatry is condemned not because of the persons who are put forward, but because of those services which pertain to demons. The things of Caesar must be rendered to Caesar. Good that he added: and the things of God to God. What then are the things of Caesar? Of course those about which the consultation was then being raised, whether the tax should be paid to Caesar or not. Therefore the Lord asked that a coin be shown to him and asked about the image, whose it was, and when he had heard that it was Caesar's, he said, render the things of Caesar to Caesar, and the things of God to God, that is, the image of Caesar to Caesar, which is on the coin, and the image of God to God, which is in man, so that you render money indeed to Caesar, yourself to God. Otherwise what will be God's, if all things are Caesar's? Therefore, you say, is the honor of God lamps before the doors and laurel on the doorposts? Not at all, because it is not an honor of God, but of him who is honored in place of God by services of this kind, as far as is in the open, with the working, which is in secret, reaching to demons. For we ought to be certain, if any are hidden by ignorance of secular literature, that there are also gods of doors among the Romans, Cardea named from hinges and Forculus from doors and Limentinus from the threshold and Janus himself from the door: and certainly we know, although the names are empty and invented, yet when they are brought into superstition, they seize to themselves demons and every unclean spirit through the bond of consecration. Otherwise demons have no name individually, but they find a name there where also a pledge is. Also among the Greeks we read that Apollo Thyraeus and Antelios are demons, guardians of doors. Therefore the Holy Spirit, foreseeing these things from the beginning, also foretold through the most ancient prophet Enoch that doors would come into superstition. For we see that other doors in the baths are adored. But if there are beings who are adored in doors, to them also lamps and laurels will pertain. You will have done to an idol whatever you will have done to a door. In this place I call to witness also by the authority of God, because it is not safe to suppress whatever has been shown to one person, certainly for the sake of all. I know a brother who was gravely rebuked through a vision on the same night, because his slaves had crowned his door when public rejoicings had suddenly been announced. And yet he himself had not crowned it or ordered it; for he had gone out earlier and on returning had rebuked the deed. To such a degree in matters of this kind even the discipline of our household is weighed before God. Therefore as far as it concerns the honors of kings or emperors, we have enough prescribed, that we ought to be in all obedience according to the apostle's precept subject to magistrates and princes and powers, but within the limits of discipline, as long as we are separated from idolatry. For this reason also that example of the three brothers went before, who, otherwise obedient toward king Nebuchadnezzar, most steadfastly rejected the honor of his image, proving that it is idolatry whatever is raised beyond the measure of human honor to the likeness of divine loftiness. So also Daniel, supported by Darius in other matters, was in office as long as he was free from the danger of discipline. For in order not to undergo that, he did not fear the royal lions more than they feared the royal fires. Therefore let them light daily lamps, for which there is no light, let them fasten to doorposts laurels soon to burn, for which fires are imminent; to them belong both testimonies of darkness and omens of punishments. You are the light of the world and a tree always green. If you have renounced temples, do not make your door a temple. I have said too little: if you have renounced brothels, do not put on your house the face of a new brothel.

pass_b_english: But, someone says, "Let your works shine" (Matthew 5:16). At present, it is our shops and doors that shine. You can now find more pagan doors without lamps and laurels than Christian ones. What should we think of this practice too? If it is honor of an idol, then without doubt honor of an idol is idolatry. If it is done for a person's sake, let us remember that all idolatry is done for a person's sake. Let us remember that all idolatry is worship offered to human beings, since even their own records show that the gods of the pagans were once human. So it makes no difference whether this superstition is offered to men of an earlier age or of this one. Idolatry is condemned not because of the persons who are put forward, but because of the services themselves, which belong to demons. "Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's" (Matthew 22:21). It is good that he added, "and to God the things that are God's." What then are Caesar's? Clearly the matter under discussion at that time: whether the tax should be paid to Caesar or not. That is why the Lord asked for a coin to be shown to him and inquired whose image it bore. When he heard that it was Caesar's, he said, "Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's" (Matthew 22:21)—that is, Caesar's image to Caesar, which is on the coin, and God's image to God, which is in the human being. So give your money to Caesar, but give yourself to God. Otherwise, what will belong to God if everything belongs to Caesar?

So, you say, are lamps before the doors and laurels on the doorposts an honor to God? Not at all, because what is honored is not God but the one who is honored in God's place by such services—as far as what is visible goes, while the working that is hidden reaches the demons. For we should be certain, if anyone is unaware through ignorance of secular literature, that the Romans even have gods of doorways: Cardea, named from hinges, and Forculus from doors, and Limentinus from the threshold, and Janus himself from the door. And we certainly know that although these names are empty and invented, when they are brought into superstition they draw demons to themselves, and every unclean spirit, through the bond of consecration. Otherwise demons have no individual names, but they find a name wherever they find a pledge. Among the Greeks too we read that Apollo Thyraeus and the Antelii are demons who guard doors. The Holy Spirit foresaw from the beginning that even doors would come into superstition, and foretold this through the most ancient prophet Enoch. For we see that other doors in the baths are also worshipped. But if there are beings worshipped at doors, then lamps and laurels belong to them. Whatever you do to a door, you have done to an idol.

At this point I call on God's authority as my witness, because it is not safe to suppress anything that has been shown to one person for the sake of all. I know a brother who was severely rebuked in a vision that same night because his servants had crowned his door when public rejoicings were suddenly announced. And yet he had not crowned it himself or ordered it; he had gone out earlier and on his return had rebuked what was done. So much are we judged before God in such matters even by the discipline of our household. Therefore, as far as honors to kings or emperors are concerned, we have enough instruction: we must be subject to magistrates and rulers and authorities in all obedience, according to the apostle's command, but within the limits of the discipline, as long as we are kept separate from idolatry. For that reason the example of the three brothers came first, who in other matters were obedient to King Nebuchadnezzar but most steadfastly refused to honor his image, proving that whatever is raised beyond the measure of human honor to the likeness of divine majesty is idolatry. So also Daniel, loyal to Darius in everything else, remained in office as long as he was free from danger to the discipline. For to avoid that danger, he feared the royal lions no more than the brothers feared the royal fires.

So let them light their lamps daily—lamps that have no light. Let them fasten laurels to their doorposts, laurels that will soon burn, with fires hanging over them. To them belong both the testimonies of darkness and the omens of punishment. You are the light of the world and a tree always green (Matthew 5:14). If you have renounced temples, do not make your door a temple. I have said too little: if you have renounced brothels, do not clothe your house with the face of a new brothel.

problems.why: Same concept (non-Christians) rendered as 'nations,' 'pagans,' and 'outsiders' interchangeably.
problems.fix: Use 'pagans' consistently or note that 'nations' = pagans.

fixed: The source 'deos nationum' uses 'nationum' for non-Christian peoples; the brief's glossary maps 'ethnici' to 'pagans' and bans 'Gentiles'/'non-Christians'. The English 'the nations' is a literal rendering that obscures the sense; changed to 'the pagans' to match the glossary's consistent term for non-Christian peoples.
